final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor offered no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key evidentiary gaps. The existing record still shows: aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred; public guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring; the multilingual customer-support segment remains exposed; Spanish-language refund guidance is below target; and there is no completed approved risk acceptance. Under the policy, that means the unresolved compliance predicate is actual pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation, unless the exposure was removed or covered by approved risk acceptance. Neither is proved here. The Actor's response is a narrower and more disciplined interpretation of the same evidence, but it remains a description of a policy-compliant path, not evidence that the path was completed. That is enough to reject a broader noncompliance theory based on unmanaged launch posture, but not enough to upgrade to compliant_with_caveats, because that category still requires the caveat to be real rather than hypothetical.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final approved model card or launch packet actually disclosed the Spanish-language refund-guidance limitation before launch.

No approved risk-acceptance record addresses continued exposure of the multilingual customer-support segment; the only artifact is an incomplete draft with a blank approver line and no mention of that exposure.

The affected multilingual customer-support segment remains eligible in the 7% rollout, so rollout percentage, rollback, regional gating, and monitoring remain mitigation controls only and do not satisfy the disclosure predicate.
The actor's narrowed position identifies a possible path to compliant_with_caveats, but the record still lacks proof that the required caveat and governance condition were actually implemented.
